text: Guys making 42k a year will hear about Elon Musk becoming a trillionaire and be like, well, he worked for it. Okay, well, you work, so where's my billion dollars? Where's my billion dollars, baby? Maybe it'll trickle down someday, who the f**k knows? Guys, you often ask me how to properly use logic in the debates. Today, I will try to show it to you using a video from this lady. Firstly, we need the premise, the main point we are debating. Otherwise, how would we know what we are even talking about? So correct me if I'm wrong, but here's how I understand it. She is reacting to Musk becoming a trillionaire and pushing back on the people who defended with he worked for it. Her point is roughly, she works, the guy on 42k works, Elon works. So if working is the reason, where is her billion? And maybe it trickles down one day, who knows? Underneath that are two ideas. First, that the reward should track the work, and if it doesn't, the system is unfair. Second, the trickle down part, that the money at the top should make its way down to other working people. That is what I'm going to test. But first, let me be precise about this trillion because it matters. It's not trillion dollars sitting in Elon's bank account. SpaceX just went public, and it is basically the value of his shares in it, on top of his Tesla shares, pushed his network past a trillion. On paper, investors were lining up to buy in, and that demand set the price. So this is not cash he's sitting on, it's the market value of companies a lot of people wanted a piece of. Keep that in mind. Here's my first and main point. Musk operates largely in a capitalistic system. And in that system, you are not exactly paid for how much you work. You are paid for how much demand there is for what you provide. That is exactly what the IPO shows. Investors were not paying for his hours. They were paying because they value what his companies make, from rockets to satellite internet. The demand set the price. So this was not really about how hard he works. And if she says that is unfair, I would point out she uses the same system. A video blogger like herself is paid not exactly by how much effort goes into the videos, but by how many views they get. Another creator could spend many more hours making videos and still get fewer views. Does that mean the money from her videos should trickle down to that person? No, of course not. I'm not saying she is the same as Musk. The scale is very different. But the principal that pays her is the one she is complaining about. So she is calling out the system that puts food on her table. Now my second point, the trickle-down part. Let us say she really believes the one who earns more should let it flow to the one who earns less, as long as they work. Then apply that to her. Around 800 million people live on less than $3 a day, and many of them probably work as much as she does. She likely earns a hundred, maybe a thousand times more. So by her own principle, why does her money not flow down to them? She can say, well, Musk has far more than a person needs, and I still need mine to get by. And that is fair, but notice what just happened. The moment she says that, she has stopped talking about work. Her reason is now how much does a person actually need, not how much a person worked, which is my first point coming back around. This was never really about effort. Not for Elon, and not for her. But hey, maybe she does give part of her income to people in extreme poverty, and good for her if so. So that is how I take a video like this apart. The most important step is the first one. Find the premise, take its strongest version, then test it. Get the frame wrong, and everything you build on top is just a noise.
